cues.text: A hard start
Ian Wright was born in 1963 in Woolwich, in London, to parents from Jamaica, and he grew up in Brockley.
His father was not around, and his mother, Nesta, brought him up.
Home was not always a happy or safe place.
Open the door.
When home feels hard, school and the people there can be a place of help.
Ian loved football, and it gave him a place to be happy.
If home feels hard, it is never your fault. Tell a teacher or another grown-up you trust.
Mr Pigden
At primary school, Ian had a teacher called Sydney Pigden.
Long before, Mr Pigden had been a pilot in the Second World War.
Mr Pigden was one of his teachers, and he noticed Ian.
Lift the flap.
Mr Pigden helped Ian learn to read and write, and he believed in him.
Ian later called him the first positive male figure in his life.
Sometimes one grown-up who believes in you can change everything.
One kind teacher can change a life. Let the helpers help you.
Two trials, two noes
As a teenager, Ian had trials at two professional clubs, Southend United and Brighton.
Neither club offered him a contract.
Being turned down can make you feel that your dream is over.
Knock on the doors.
Ian kept playing anyway, in Sunday league football.
He became the top scorer in his league.
He was playing for fun, but he was getting better every week.
Keep playing for the love of it, even when the big doors stay shut.
A late start
Ian played for a small club, Greenwich Borough.
Then, in August 1985, when he was twenty-one, he signed for Crystal Palace.
Most new professional players are much younger.
Climb the steps.
Ian worked hard and scored lots of goals.
In 1989, he scored 24 league goals and helped Palace win promotion to the top division.
It is never too late to start. Your path can be different from everyone else’s.
Goals for Arsenal
In 1991, Ian joined Arsenal, and he played for England too.
He scored 185 goals for Arsenal, more than anyone before him.
Years later, in 2005, Thierry Henry beat his record.
Arsenal paid a club-record fee for him.
Flip the scoreboard.
With Arsenal, Ian won the FA Cup, the League Cup and the league title.
The young man who started late had become one of the best strikers in England.
Hard work and joy together can take you a very long way.
Thank you, Mr Pigden
Ian had been told that Mr Pigden had died.
But in 2005, on a BBC television programme, his old teacher walked in to meet him.
Ian was so happy that he cried.
They hugged, and the moment was watched by people all over the country.
Lift the photo frame.
Ian later dedicated his life story, a book he wrote in 2016, to Mr Pigden.
He never forgot the teacher who had believed in him when he was a boy.
Remember the people who helped you, and tell them thank you.
